title: Fidelity packages and customer migration playbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:

This document defines a new set of "fidelity packages" — opinionated, billable bundles that map observable service fidelity (latency SLOs, token quality tiers, model quantization profile) to pricing and an explicit migration path for existing customers. It is intended for product managers, pricing, sales engineering, and platform engineering responsible for packaging, rollout and monitoring.

Goals and success metrics:

- Reduce customer support friction during quality/cost tradeoff changes by providing explicit, named packages.
- Provide deterministic economics so customers can reason about cost vs. fidelity before migrating.
- Enable safe automated migrations for early-adopter pilots and a manual migration path for enterprise customers.
- Success metrics (90-day target): 60% of eligible customers offered an automated migration opt-in, <3% regression alerts after migration, and +10% ARR retention attributable to clearer packaging.

Audience:

- Product and GTM: define packaging and commercial terms.
- Platform and Runtime: implement routing, throttles, and telemetry mapping.
- SRE and Observability: define SLOs, alerts, and dashboards used during migration.
- Sales Engineering / Customer Success: run migrations and validate customer requirements.

Context and rationale:

Redwood currently offers a set of knobs (batching, quantization profile, model variant routing, caching) that can be combined into many configurations. Customers repeatedly ask for an opinionated, predictable set of choices they can buy and commit to. Fidelity packages reduce cognitive load, accelerate procurement, and make rollback and support processes repeatable.

Package definitions (names and components):

| Package name | Latency SLO (p95) | Model fidelity profile | Quantization | Auto-batching target | Default cache retention | Typical workload types | Price band |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Standard | 200 ms | Redwood-1 (baseline) | int8 | 8–12 reqs | 30s prefix | chat UIs, short prompts | $ |
| Business | 120 ms | Redwood-1.2 (improved sampling) | int8-mixed | 4–8 reqs | 60s prefix | higher-traffic chat, customer support | $$ |
| High-Fidelity | 60 ms | Redwood-2 (higher-context tokens, better sampling) | fp16 | 2–4 reqs | 120s prefix | document generation, summarization | $$$ |
| Economy | 500 ms | Redwood-lite (smaller variant) | int4 | 16+ reqs | 0s | bulk embeddings, offline batching | $ (discount) |

Note: Price band values above are placeholders — the final commercial SKU will map these bands to defined token/unit prices and any minimum commitments.

Mapping runtime knobs to package guarantees:

- Routing: packages are implemented as route policies that select a matching model variant and runtime tier.
- Quantization: package picks an approved quantization profile; migrations must validate output-quality delta with a regression test suite.
- Batching: each package sets a target batching window and max batch size; SLOs define acceptable latency percentiles at that batching level.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache TTLs and hit policy are set per package to meet cost targets.

Migration playbook (summary steps):

1. Identify eligible customers
   - Eligibility criteria: active usage > 100k tokens/month, no open quality regressions, model family compatibility.
2. Pre-migration validation (automated)
   - Run a per-tenant synthetic workload generator (seeded with customer's prompt-set) against the target package to collect: token-cost delta, latency distribution, sample outputs.
   - Compute quality deltas using customer's golden-set evaluation; threshold for auto-approve: BLEU/ROUGE/LLR equivalent within configured tolerance or fewer than 5% content-regression alerts.
3. Offer staged opt-in
   - Email + Console: present predicted cost delta and expected SLO improvements. Include an explicit rollback window (default 72 hours) and a one-click opt-in.
4. Canary migration (automated)
   - 5% traffic for 48 hours, collect metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, quality regressions, error rate).
   - Gate criteria: no SLO violation > 1 minute of continuous breach, error rate < 0.2% above baseline, quality regressions below threshold.
5. Gradual ramp
   - 25% for 24 hours, then 50% for 24 hours, then 100% if metrics stable.
6. Post-migration audit
   - Generate a migration report with telemetry, cost delta, and any regression findings. Tag customer account with package id and chosen rollback strategy.

Manual migration path (enterprise customers):

- SJ (Sales/SE) runs a validated lab migration with the customer present.
- Use an extended canary (7–14 days) and provide manual rollback controls.
- Document contractual changes (if any) and update the billing configuration after completion.

SLO / Billing mapping and contract implications:

- Each package maps to a named SLO bundle (e.g., "Business-120ms-v1"). Contracts reference the SLO bundle by name; SLA credits are tied to the bundle’s p95 latency and error-rate thresholds.
- Price mapping table (example):

| Package | Token price multiplier | Minimum monthly commit | SLA credit basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Economy | 0.6x | $0 | None (best-effort) |
| Standard | 1.0x | $0 | p95 latency 200ms, <0.5% errors |
| Business | 1.6x | $5k | p95 latency 120ms, <0.3% errors |
| High-Fidelity | 2.8x | $25k | p95 latency 60ms, <0.1% errors |

Telemetry and observability requirements:

- New dashboards per package: latency distribution, token cost per-request, quantization hit/miss, model-variant switches, cache hit rate, regression-alert count.
- Traces must include package_id, model_variant, quant_profile, batch_size, and cache_ttl to correlate regressions.
- Alerting rules:
  - Package SLO breach alert (p95 > target for 5m) -> Platform on-call and Product on-call.
  - Regression alert (customer evaluation failing) -> Product owner, SE, and Customer Success.

Regression testing harness (requirements):

1. Per-tenant gold-set runner with 1,000 prompts representative of heavy paths.
2. Automated scoring: semantic similarity (embedding-based), hallucination detectors, and business-rule checks.
3. Threshold configuration per package and per customer tier.

Rollout timeline and milestones (proposed Q1 2028):

- Week 1–2: finalize package SLO definitions and pricing multipliers. Owners: Product / Pricing.
- Week 3–4: implement route policies and telemetry tags. Owners: Platform / Runtime.
- Week 5–6: build migration automation and the per-tenant synthetic validator. Owners: Eng-Platform, Eng-Serving-Runtime.
- Week 7–8: pilot with 10 opt-in customers. Owners: Customer Success / SE.
- Week 9–12: iterate on playbook and scale to broader cohort. Owners: Product / SRE.

Testing checklist (pre-launch):

- [ ] Package telemetry surfaced in Console and Dashboards.
- [ ] Automated regression runner validated on historical migrations.
- [ ] Billing mappings for packages added to billing pipeline (test invoices).
- [ ] Rollback automation verified in staging.
- [ ] SE runbook and customer-facing FAQ drafted.

Appendix: CLI examples and JSON snippets

Example: attach package to a route via CLI

$ redwood routes update --route-id r_12345 --package Business

Expected response (JSON):

{
  "route_id": "r_12345",
  "package": "Business",
  "slo_bundle": "Business-120ms-v1",
  "effective_at": "2028-02-14T00:00:00Z"
}
